payload.answer:
Typically performance problems are exhibited by system slowness, record locks, high CPU, slow command response time, system freezing up, etc.. etc.. Do a top (or topas) on your system, look for the top processes consuming high CPU. If you see any db2 processes, look in the regular DB2 db2diag.log for messages related to DB2 errors. If you see high CPU usage or performance issues on the DB2 server running the octigate database, you have few options on how to fix this.
The most common symptom we've seen when performance problems happen is when the number of records in the METHOD/REQUEST/MEMORYDATA is high (approx. 5M to 7M or higher records in any table), the subsequent inserts/updates into the tables gets much slower leading to performance issues. [S1]

source_lineage.excerpt:
Typically performance problems are exhibited by system slowness, record locks, high CPU, slow command response time, system freezing up, etc.. etc.. Do a top (or topas) on your system, look for the top processes consuming high CPU. If you see any db2 processes, look in the regular DB2 db2diag.log for messages related to DB2 errors. If you see high CPU usage or performance issues on the DB2 server running the octigate database, you have few options on how to fix this.
The most common symptom we've seen when performance problems happen is when the number of records in the METHOD/REQUEST/MEMORYDATA is high (approx. 5M to 7M or higher records in any table), the subsequent inserts/updates into the tables gets much slower leading to performance issues.

The user must be either of the following types: 

• A DB2 administrator user (for example, db2admin on Windows operating systems, or db2inst1 on Linux or AIX operating systems) 

• A database user specific to the ITCAM Management Server database that has at least the following authorizations: 

o Connect to the database 

o Create tables 

o Create index 

o Perform select, insert, update, and delete operations on the tables in the database.

 ITCAM ITCAMfAD ITCAM for App Diagnostics

octigate tables MS schema SchemaSpy 71 CAMADAL CAMADINST TECHNOTE (FAQ)

THIS DOCUMENT APPLIES ONLY TO THE FOLLOWING LANGUAGE VERSION(S):
 US English 

QUESTION
 Is there an easy listing of all octigate tables available in ITCAM for Application Diagnostics v7.1? 

ANSWER
There's no built-in schema tool available to get a listing of the octigate tables and their relationship hierarchies. You'll have to use one of the many tools available on the Internet to create a schema listing of the octigate database. One of the common ones I've seen used is SchemaSpy available here:
http://schemaspy.sourceforge.net/ [http://schemaspy.sourceforge.net/]

ANSWER
Ideally, you should set up your ITCAM database (OCTIGATE) pruning and optimization when you create the Managing Server. Click here [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/tivihelp/v24r1/index.jsp?topic=%2Fcom.ibm.itcamfad.doc_7101%2FMS_install_guide%2Fopgd0021008724.html] for details on optimizing the database which can be found in the Managing Server Installation Guide. 
In the case of an extremely large OCTIGATE database that has not been trimmed by the datatrim script on a regular basis, you may want to consider dropping and rebuilding the following 4 tables. 

request 
method 
serverstats 
gc_data 

These 4 tables are usually the big ones. Recreating them will not harm ITCAM in any way other than the fact that the data will be lost.
